outside.topic: Who may redeem, and whether anyone must
outside.says: A discretionary request for USDC or 'another mutually agreed form of value', which the operator may answer by pointing to on-chain liquidity. Stays in the Terms of Service.

outside.topic: Freeze, clawback, burn, compulsory redemption and fees
outside.says: The Terms reserve all of them without notice or consent, at a value that may be nil, and fees 'at the token, smart-contract, or program level' without any duty to explain them. Stays in the terms; the chain shows the capability.
BVI law, 30 days' negotiation, then LCIA arbitration seated in London on an individual basis, with BVI courts as fallback. The BVI is also on the same document's Prohibited Jurisdictions list.
No external price exists for the private companies; the token price diverged from the issuer's own mark in both directions on 2026-09-18 (OPENAI 11.4% above, SPACEX 21.9% below).

ingredients.label: A named legal entity behind the mint's authority
A named holding entity's holdings under A, under 90 days
An independent reserve attestation, under 90 days

verdict.summary: Every type the structure needs exists (T, A, H, an audited certification), but nobody is named to sign any of them except an anonymous multisig, and the custodian and attestor are withheld by policy. What the holder has, a discretionary request with no entitlement against an unnamed counterparty, is neither an issuer obligation nor an ownership interest, so the core of the position cannot be said. The mints are Token-2022, so the reader cannot show the clawback, fee and rebase powers that matter most.
